history.summary: Hilltop shrine of Pahari Maa (goddess of the hill, a form of Durga) at Golpahari near Parsudih, just outside Jamshedpur city near Tatanagar railway station. Legend: around 1900, Ramadai (Ramdai) Devi, who had come from Pratapgarh (Uttar Pradesh) with her daughter Yashoda and lived in a hut at the hill's foot, dreamt of a stone idol with two eyes carved on it atop the hill; she found it and began worshipping it, later building the temple. Ramadai worshipped until 1938, her daughter-in-law Shanti Devi until 2004, and Shanti Devi's daughter-in-law Pushpa Tiwari maintains it now; the temple is known for its tradition of women priests and has an idol of Ramadai Devi herself. The hill (~600 ft, 80-225 steps) also holds smaller temples to Shiva, Hanuman, Kali, Durga, Jagannath and Ganesha, and offers panoramic city views. CSV town 'Jamshedpur' is coarse - corrected to Parsudih/Golpahari, Jamshedpur.

name: Golpahari Mandir (Gol Pahari Mandir)
town_description: Jamshedpur, known as the Steel City of India, is the largest city in Jharkhand. Founded by Jamsetji Tata as a planned industrial town around Tata Steel (TISCO), the settlement was called Sakchi until it was renamed Jamshedpur in 1919. The city sits at the confluence of the Kharkai and Subarnarekha rivers in East Singhbhum district, and its neighbourhoods (Telco, Golmuri, Sakchi, Kadma, Parsudih, Sidhgora) grew around Tata Steel and its subsidiary companies. Parsudih lies on the city's edge near Tatanagar Junction railway station.

travel.railway: Tatanagar Junction, very close (~1-2 km, Parsudih side; verify)
travel.road: Reached via Parsudih by auto/taxi; ~80-225 steps climb to the hilltop - no vehicles to the top, difficult for elderly visitors

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (winter); Navratri and Ram Navami are the major festival periods
visitor_information.opening_hours: 06:00 AM - 06:00 PM all days (per Velpu; verify). Climbing the steps takes 15-20 minutes; small puja-material shops at the base
